text:
Your lawyer is right. Border control at Ben Gurion Airport once stopped my non-Israeli wife when she was traveling with me, even though we don’t live in Israel and were just there for a visit. They suspected she was trying to obtain legal status in Israel without going through the proper process from abroad. If we hadn’t gotten prior authorization for her visit through the embassy, she would’ve been sent back.

In your case, since misrad hapnim is already aware of your girlfriend, the visa waiver for EU citizens no longer automatically applies, and she’ll most likely be flagged at border control. They might require you to pay a security deposit of 30000–50000 shekels to let her in, but there’s also a good chance they’ll simply deport her. Oh, and if there are no direct flights back that day, she’ll have an extremely doubtful pleasure of spending a night in a deportation detention facility.

So your options are either to get explicit permission from misrad hapnim for her to visit you, or to go visit her yourself. Under no circumstances would I recommend just boarding a plane and hoping for the best. It could turn into a very unpleasant experience and even result in an entry ban.
